PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: ward-adam
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Wardrobe guard: transfer only textile rendering, light response, practical aging, and filmic material quality. Do not introduce white burial linen, blood, sandals, or a body identity unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
ROUGH-SPUN EARTH-TONE GARMENTS — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: COSTUME CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, FIT, DAMAGE, AND CONTINUITY.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic wardrobe ingredients isolation sheet for Adam the First Man Freed in JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL — production costume reference of his rough-spun earth-tone garments only, locked across every panel for continuity on the liberation of the first soul from Hell's inner chamber. Present the same costume construction in four panels: (1) frontal three-quarter worn view on Adam's body silhouette, (2) full-body standing costume display, (3) side profile showing drape, hem, and layer thickness, (4) rear costume view of back yoke, shoulder seams, and hanging fabric fall. One human face only on the front of the head where a figure is shown; no second face, no rear face, no mask faces. Photoreal live-action biblical epic wardrobe reference, not fashion editorial, not illustration, not CGI cartoon.

SUBJECT / WEARER LOCK (for scale and fit only): Ancient first man, approximately 6'2" (188 cm), thin elongated frame with residual underlying strength from millennia of captivity. When the figure is visible, he is an elderly Mediterranean-to-Near-Eastern patriarch with long winter-frost white hair and full white beard, pale dust-filmed skin, dark tear-wet eyes — but the hero subject of this sheet is the garments, not portrait glamour. Hands clean and anatomically exact. No jewelry, no crown, no staff, no belt buckle, no sandals if footwear is bare or mere wrapped scraps — accessories none; stripped of all worldly possessions per continuity.

PRIMARY GARMENT — ROUGH-SPUN TUNIC: A simple ankle-length or mid-calf rough-spun tunic of hand-woven plant-fiber cloth (coarse linen/hemp blend feel), undyed and earth-toned. Color map locked: dry clay brown, faded ochre, ash-grey taupe, and sun-bleached sand beige mottled together as if the cloth has aged in subterranean dust rather than sunlight. Weave is openly visible — thick irregular handspun threads, slight slubs, uneven warp tension, small repairs and re-stitched tears with darker matching fiber. Construction is primitive and humble: square-cut body panels, dropped shoulder seams, simple side gores for minimal movement, a rough V- or slit neckline without collar, short-to-three-quarter sleeves ending frayed above the wrist bones so thin forearms and chain-scarred wrists can read clearly when chains break. No embroidery, no dye patterns, no royal purple, no blue, no gold thread — pure earth palette of the first father before kingship or priesthood.

LAYERING / UNDERLAYER: Optional thin inner wrap or remnant under-tunic of even more threadbare pale earth linen, peeking only at the neck slit and lower hem where the outer cloth has worn through. Outer tunic hangs loose on a gaunt body, fabric pooling slightly at the waist without a formal belt — if any waist binding exists it is a crude twisted cord of the same plant fiber, knotted simply, not leather tooling or metal. Overall silhouette is vertical, elongated, penitential, and ancient — the garment of a soul who has waited since Eden, not a soldier or king.

WEAR, DIRT, AND CONTINUITY DAMAGE MAP (must match across all four views): Fabric worn translucent-thin at elbows, knees, and high-wear chest folds; multiple horizontal stress tears along the lower third from kneeling and chain drag; frayed hems hanging in irregular soft tassels of broken warp threads. Surface contamination: centuries of hell-chamber dust — fine grey ash film in weave valleys, darker soot streaks along side seams, pale mineral salt crust at hem from moisture and chain-floor contact, subtle iron-oxide rust smudges at mid-forearm and waist where corroded hell chains pressed against cloth for ages. When divine gold light arrives in the liberation beat, dust on raised folds catches warm amber highlights while recessed folds stay cold blue-shadowed. No fresh bright blood on Adam's garments (blood continuity belongs to Jesus); only dust, ash, rust contact, and tear-paths of salt if moisture from weeping has tracked onto the upper chest cloth. Continuity lock: same tear map, same ash density, same fray pattern on every panel — front tears align with rear tears at corresponding body zones.

POSE / PRESENTATION PER PANEL: Panel one — three-quarter worn portrait framing from mid-thigh up, garment clearly reading neckline, sleeve fray, chest wear, and shoulder drape while Adam kneels or half-rises in the moment of freedom (tears cutting dust on face if face is shown, hands trembling open). Panel two — full-body standing or rising from kneel, complete tunic length, hem clearance above bare or rag-wrapped feet, empty hands, no props. Panel three — pure side profile isolating fabric thickness at side seam, how cloth hangs off the ribcage, sleeve silhouette, and rear hem drift. Panel four — rear costume construction: back of neck slit, center-back seam or seamless loom panel, shoulder-blade wear patches, long fall of fabric to the heels, complete white hair crown and rear hair only if head is included — never a face on the back of the head. Mannequin-style neutral pose is acceptable if identity is locked to Adam's body proportions; prefer soft living drape over stiff dress-form plastics.

ENVIRONMENT CONTEXT (subtle, not a full location plate): Soft production-studio void or shallow hell-chamber suggestion only — cold blue torch spill ~2000K as fill from one side and early divine warm amber ~3200–4500K key from the opposite side, matching the inner-chamber liberation grade (warm amber against cold blue shadows). Thin volumetric dust motes in the light. No full 100-ft gate, no crowds, no sword of light, no modern stands or hangers with branding.

LIGHTING AND CAMERA: Physically coherent dual-key cinematic lighting; soft large key from upper front-left in warm amber, cool blue rim from rear-right suggesting remaining hell torches before full transformation. Gentle specular on raised linen threads; subsurface glow through thin worn patches. Camera language: sharp production-reference multi-panel sheet, each panel equivalent to roughly 50–85mm portrait / 35–50mm full-body feel, shallow DOF only at panel edges so fabric texture stays readable. Aspect and layout clean four-quadrant or horizontal strip without borders, captions, labels, arrows, or measurement callouts. Color grade: desaturated earth browns and greys in the cloth, warm amber highlights on dust peaks, residual cold blue in shadow folds — biblical epic photoreal, sacred and humble tone.

TEXTURE AND MATERIAL TRUTH: Emphasize tactile rough-spun weave, broken fiber ends, dust-caked valleys between threads, soft collapsed drape of aged cloth, no synthetic sheen, no polyester, no modern stitching machines, no zippers, no buttons, no snaps, no printed logos. Hands and any visible skin photoreal and anatomically correct. Single face only on the front of the head. No modern objects, no smartphones, no studio clapboards, no hang tags, no barcodes, no readable text, no watermarks, no UI, no graphic borders. Continuity repeat: Adam's rough-spun earth-tone tunic — clay-ochre-taupe-beige handwoven plant fiber, worn translucent at joints, frayed sleeves and hem, ash and rust-chain contact stains, no accessories — identical construction and damage map on frontal three-quarter, full-body, side, and rear panels for JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL wardrobe lock.
